description: rivr is an R package for calculating open-channel hydraulic states, maintained as a teaching and research tool. It offers functions for normal and critical depth, flow and channel geometry, gradually varied water-surface profiles and unsteady flood-wave routing. Users supply channel shape, flow, roughness, boundary conditions and time or distance settings; outputs are calculated depths and profiles for the chosen channel. Geography, reach length and simulation step are defined by the user, with no bundled national river network. GPL-3.0 source is available through GitHub and CRAN, with documentation and an R Journal article. Although its README calls it educational, this is a documented functional package, not a single course exercise repository. A limitation is that simple one-dimensional channel calculations do not capture a full two-dimensional urban floodplain or calibrated network without more data. rivr can support flood-wave and river-capacity analysis. The catalogue's model-raven is a broader catchment hydrology framework for comparison; no direct coupling was tested. No R package was installed.
inputs: Channel geometry, flow, roughness and boundary conditions
